The infobox gives 'disestablished 1598' because the county survived as a title of Aragonese princes (Peter, Alfonso, Martin ... 1322-1598), not as a state.

rulers.name: Raymond I
rulers.note: First independent count of Pallars and Ribagorza 'from 872 until his death'; the Raymond I page gives no death date, 920 is the Ribagorza page's end of his rule. Ribagorza went to his two eldest sons, Miró and Bernard Unifred (Humfred), Pallars to the two youngest.

rulers.note: '920-950/955'; Miró ruled jointly from 920; through his marriage to Toda Galíndez they were sometimes counts of Sobrarbe.

rulers.name: William Isarn
rulers.note: Held a portion after the 1010 partition 'following intervention by Sancho García of Castile'; Mayor García claimed the county 1010-1025 with Raymond III of Pallars, divorced 1019/20.

rulers.name: Sancho III of Pamplona

rulers.note: 'Ruled first William Isarn's portion, then the entire county by conquest and submission.'

correction.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

keyframe_review.note: 866-874, 15,408 km2. This is the Kingdom of Pamplona's 860 shape, cell for cell (59 of 59 cells: Navarra, Álava, Gipuzkoa, Biscay), not a county in the central Pyrenees. The Ribagorza page gives the county 'Established 872' under Raymond I (872-920) with its seat at Benabarre in 'the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena, and Noguera Ribagorzana'. The Pamplona part is carried by kingdom-of-pamplona_866; Ribagorza proper is the circle from 872.

correction.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

keyframe_review.note: 875-921, 20,877 km2 (the loss of much of Ribagorza to al-Tawil of Huesca in 907, including Roda and Montpedrós, is in the ledger): Pamplona's 59 cells plus 23 cells of the central Pyrenees (lat 42.09-42.75 N, lon -0.34-0.64 E, centred 42.4 N, 0.2 E), which are west of the Ribagorza valleys the page describes and take in Sobrarbe. Pamplona's part goes to kingdom-of-pamplona_866; Ribagorza keeps the valleys. The page does not give the area.

The land is still Ribagorza's, but the ledger gives it to Pamplona (1018 portion, 1025 the rest).

keyframe_review.note: 1028-1033, 85,501 km2 (Navarre, Aragon, La Rioja, Burgos, Soria, Cantabria, 73 Catalan cells): this is Sancho III's kingdom of Pamplona after Castile (1028 on the Navarre page, 1027 on the Sancho III page) and the Pisuerga-Cea; see kingdom-of-pamplona_1028. Ribagorza stays the valleys, in Sancho's hands.

After 1035 'Gonzalo ... in control of the counties of Sobrarbe and Ribagorza' (Sancho III page): Ribagorza and Sobrarbe are the shape from 1035 (1034 itself is still Sancho's).

region.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

ledger.note: 872: Raymond I seizes Pallars and Ribagorza. After Bernard II of Toulouse was assassinated he 'seized authority for himself in Pallars and Ribagorza' and ruled them as first independent count 'from 872 until his death' (infobox 'Established 872'). The land is the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana.

region.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

ledger.note: 907: Muhammad al-Tawil of Huesca takes much of Ribagorza. Ribagorza lost 'to Muhammad al-Tawil of Huesca in 907', including Roda and Montpedrós, after which Raymond 'ruled mainly Pallars'; Lubb ibn Muhammad had attacked him in 904 and taken 700 prisoners. The extent of 'much of' Ribagorza is not mapped.

region.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

ledger.note: 920: Ribagorza is back in Raymond's family. The Raymond I page says only that on his death Ribagorza went to Miró and Bernard Unifred; it does not say how Ribagorza was recovered from al-Tawil after 907.

region.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

ledger.note: 920: Raymond I's lands are divided among his four sons. 'After his death, his lands were divided among four sons'; Pallars and Ribagorza part, and Miró and Bernard I Humfred rule Ribagorza jointly.

region.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

ledger.note: 1010: Ribagorza is partitioned. William Isarn held a portion 'after a partition following intervention by Sancho García of Castile'; Mayor García claimed the county with her husband Raymond III of Pallars until their divorce in 1019/20.

region.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

ledger.note: 1018: Sancho III of Pamplona takes William Isarn's portion. 'In 1018, William Isarn tried to solidify his control over the Arán valley, but was killed. Sancho then took his portion.'

region.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

ledger.note: 1025: the rest of Ribagorza submits to Sancho III. The rival claim was 'finally resolved in 1025 when Mayor retired to a Castilian convent'; Sancho 'ruled ... the entire county by conquest and submission' (Ribagorza page, 1018-1035).

zones.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana, seat at Benabarre

wars.outcome: Lubb ibn Muhammad al-Qasawi attacks Raymond I in 904 and takes 700 prisoners, among them his son Isarn; in 907 Muhammad al-Tawil of Huesca takes much of Ribagorza, including Roda and Montpedrós. In 905 Raymond collaborated with Alfonso III and al-Qasawi to put Sancho Garcés I on the throne of Pamplona.

wars.outcome: The 1010 partition between William Isarn and Mayor García (with Raymond III of Pallars), under Sancho García of Castile's intervention, ends with William Isarn killed in 1018 and Mayor's retirement in 1025; Sancho III of Pamplona holds the whole county from 1025 until 1035.

notes: Cliopatria's 'County of Ribagorza' row (866-1084, 11 shapes) is mostly the Kingdom of Pamplona/Navarre: the 866-874 shape equals Pamplona's 860 shape cell for cell; 875-1027 adds 23-28 cells of the central Pyrenees (Sobrarbe and Ribagorza) to it, plus Aragon's 15 cells from 922; 1028-1033 and 1034-1039 are Sancho III's expanded kingdom (85,501 and 171,828 km2); 1040-1084 are García III's and Sancho IV's Navarre. Verdicts: adjust where a Pyrenean part exists, wrong for 1028, 1034, 1046 and 1072; the kingdom-of-pamplona dossier carries the new keyframes 866 to 1054. Ribagorza proper is drawn as a 40 km circle on 42.35 N, 0.55 E (the valleys the page names; the gazetteer has no Ribagorza, Sobrarbe or Benabarre), a reading. The state ends in 1045, not 1084 or 1598 (the infobox's 1598 is the title surviving as an Aragonese appanage). Not settled: how Ribagorza was held 872-1010 beyond the count lists (no Muslim or Frankish event is dated on the pages opened); the extent of William Isarn's portion in 1010-1018; the Arán valley; Barbastro and Graus (not on the page). Pallars (Cliopatria 875-1014) and Ribagorza were ruled together by Raymond I 872-920. Names needed in the gazetteer: Ribagorza, Sobrarbe, Benabarre, Aínsa, Arán valley. Page budget: 4 of 5 pages used (Ribagorza, Raymond I, Sancho III, Navarre). Muhammad al-Tawil of Huesca (Banu Qasi page: 911 'Abd Allah and al-Tawil attack Pamplona') needs a place in the Upper March dossiers. The Raymond I page also has Raymond 'purchasing Zaragoza' in 884, 'only to have it immediately reconquered by the Caliphate' (the emirate's 884 gain).
